requirements.text: `Progress` is the widget-hosting operational summary tab.
`History` and `Ledger` should remain separate with distinct purposes.
Evidence view should be split into separate `Evidence` and `Artifacts` panes.
Cross-tab deep links should carry selection/filter/focus context, not just tab switches.
Blocked states should always expose reason, owner, blocked duration, and next step.

decisions.text: Keep Orchestrator tabs separate as `Progress`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger`.
`Seams` should be hierarchical seam-first, package-second, with node drill-in.
Prefer a broader Progress-widget catalog and let users hide what they do not need.
Default Progress-widget drill targets are deterministic and tab-specific.
Keep right-side inspectors summary/action-oriented and open dense objects in full-record views.
Keep expert/canonical terms stable and derive simpler labels later where needed.
Chat thread should only surface situations requiring user resolution or decision.

data_shapes.text: Progress widget set includes Run Status, Current Activity, Attention/Blockers, Seam Health, Package Activity, Promotion Queue, Worktree Lanes, Account/Usage Pressure, Recent Major Events, Overseer Activity, Corroboration Queue, Recovery State, Throughput/Capacity.
Widget-to-tab routing map defines fixed drill targets (e.g., Run Status->History, Promotion Queue->Ledger, Corroboration Queue->Evidence).
Node Graph detail inspector fields include provider/model/effort/persona/account, usage/tokens/cost, worker policy, retry/review/promotion, lane/worktree/snapshot, and linked evidence/artifacts.
History stores chronological execution narrative; Ledger stores structured durable inspection records.

Canonical state/action labels include `Locally Complete`, `Seam Complete`, `Completion Blocked`, `Weak Integration`, `Promotion Blocked`, `Promotion Revoked`, `Corroboration Requested`, `Graph Patch Requested`, and `Graph Patch Applied`.
Blocked ownership labels are normalized as `Runtime`, `Package Overseer`, `Seam Overseer`, `Corroboration`, `Graph Patch`, `Recovery`, `User`, `External Resource`.
Alert levels are separated into `Info`, `Warning`, `Attention`, and `Action Required`.
Canonical event families remain stable as `seam.*`, `package.*`, `node.*`, `promotion.*`, `corroboration.*`, `graph_patch.*`, `recovery.*`, `account.*`.

routing_rules.text: Node Graph evidence/artifact links deep-link into Evidence with target selection/filter.

verification_rules.text: Graph-detail evidence/artifact links should deep-link to Evidence with preserved target/filter context.
Cross-tab deep links should preserve selection/filter/focus context.
`Weak Integration` should be summarized and grouped under readable concern headings.
Package issues roll up to seam concerns only when they cross package/seam/user-visible boundaries or affect seam-completion truth.
Revocation and reopen semantics should be explicit and visible.

owner_consumer_obligations.text: Seams UI should present `Weak Integration` with clear grouped concern headings (Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, Design).
Completion status must distinguish `Locally Complete`, `Available to Seam`, and `Seam Complete`.
Promotion boundaries must be surfaced as `Lane to Package`, `Package to Seam`, and `Seam Completion`.
Dashboard presents summary/urgency while Orchestrator provides detailed operational alert context.

stale_retirement_items.text: Retire `Tiers` tab in favor of seam/package-oriented `Seams` tab.
Retire default node-list shape in Seams in favor of summary/problem-focused drill-ins.

open_questions.text: Seam/package-oriented tab likely named `Seams`, but naming remained open in earlier notes.
Operator visibility split is introduced but details are not fully captured in the shard extract.

doc_hints.text: Prefer precise canonical terms in runtime/docs and defer simplified labels to targeted UX surfaces.
